procedural_matters: The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
ITA 12 was represented by Antonio Braucci.
NOR 55 came to the hearing after ITA 12 has given their evidence. The hearing continued in NOR 55's presence.
NOR 55 was represented by Arild Heldal.
Michał Gonciarz (POL 2) presented evidence during the hearing as a witness for ITA 12.
The international jury presented video evidence.
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 6-7 knots of wind and a decreasing swell.
ITA 12 and NOR 55 were sailing on port tack, on the last reach to the finishing line. ITA 12 was clear astern and to leeward of NOR 55.
NOR 55 was approaching the line sailing a higher course and pointing to windward of the pin end.
Some other boats were clear ahead of both ITA 12 and NOR 55.
When NOR 55 was 2.5 metres away from the mark she bore away. At that moment, ITA 12 established an overlap to leeward of NOR 55 at a distance of 1 metre.

A few seconds later, while crossing the finishing line and when NOR 55 was 1.5 metres beside the mark, she luffed sharply and there was immediately a contact between NOR 55's starboard edge of the stern and ITA 12's port side of the hull.
The contact resulted in a scratch on ITA 12's deck and a small spider crack on the hull of the boat.
conclusions: Since the boats have finished, but not cleared the finishing line and marks, the boats were still racing.
NOR 55 to windward failed to keep clear of ITA 12 to leeward and broke RRS 11.
Since NOR 55 was not sailing within the mark-room she was entitled to, she is not exonerated for her breach.
NOR 55 did not avoid contact when it was reasonably possible and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for ITA 12 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with NOR 55 when it became clear that NOR 55 was not keeping clear. ITA 12 did not break RRS 14(a).
